newsitem.title: UK: Dollar charts point higher as key hurdles dissolve.
newsitem.headline: Dollar charts point higher as key hurdles dissolve.

text.p: The dollar charts are pointing to an extension of recent gains against the mark and yen after Friday's test above key chart levels, said technical analysts.

Dollar/mark breached key psychological resistance at 1.85 marks today for the first time since November 1989 while dollar/yen poked above its major target at 119 yen. A sustained break above these levels could herald substantial gains for the dollar, said analysts.
Dollar/mark popped up to a session high of 1.8570 marks in afternoon Europe before edging back slightly while dollar/yen touched 119.17 in earlier trade.

Above the 1.85 marks level, analysts said there was little in its way before 1.86 marks, another round-figure barrier, and then the November 1989 high of 1.8690 which is reinforced by an old resistance zone in the 1.87 area.
"A break of 1.85 would confirm a bull flag with targets up to around 1.8775," said Alan Dunne, technical analyst at Bank of America in London.
This bull flag formation outlines the dollar/mark's two-week consolidation after its break above the 1.82 level and echoes a pattern it followed when it broke above 1.78 marks in mid-July.
Analysts see clearance of 1.85 and a close above here as the catalyst for a similar leg higher.

"A sustained break of 1.85 would inject some confidence for a push to 1.8600, 1.8750 and bring 1.9000 into the frame going forward," said Brian Kiely, treasury technician at Royal Bank of Scotland in London.
However, Kiely also sees the current dollar strength as possibly the last flurry of a mature trend. "Friday is a wild card for currencies and the picture could quickly deteriorate."
Dollar/yen made a brief stab above a key resistance point at 119 yen after its attempt to break through here earlier this week.

But today's foray higher was brief and the 119 area, a 50-percent retracement of dollar/yen's early-May to mid-June decline, is still expected to provide a tough sticking point for a dollar move higher.

Like dollar/mark, chartists see a lot of empty space before the next significant target, in this case 120 yen. An ascending channel top from early July cuts in around 119.70 but will be around 120 yen at the beginning of next week, said Ian Stannard, technical analyst at Chase Investment Bank in London.
As well as being a round-figure, psychological hurdle, the 120 level provided a tough resistance point on dollar/yen's rise early this year and support for the late February/early March trough.
"If we get to 120, given the significance of this level we could get a near-term pullback to the 119 level," said Chase's Stannard.
Above 120, the 121 area is the next upside target, being a support area from mid-February and early-March and, more significantly, a 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement of the May-June downmove.
